# Twelve Shiny companions to the labs
::: {.lead}
Apps that let you turn the dials on the most important ideas in the
curriculum and watch the consequences live.
:::
:::

The apps complement the labs. Each lab teaches you the mechanics of a
method on a fixed dataset; the corresponding app lets you wiggle every
parameter and watch the answer change. Build intuition first, then
read the lab — or read the lab first and use the app to stress-test
your understanding.

::: {.callout-tip}
**Source:** every app is a single `app.R` in
[`shiny/<app-name>/`](https://github.com/CTTIR/courses/tree/main/shiny)
on GitHub. They are designed for self-hosted Shiny Server but run
locally with one command:

```bash
R -e 'shiny::runApp("shiny/clt-explorer", launch.browser = TRUE)'
```
:::

The links below open each app’s source and instructions. No public Shiny
host is configured here. Restore the project environment as described in
[Get started](get_started.qmd), then replace `clt-explorer` in the command
above with the desired app folder. GitHub Pages cannot execute R apps.

## Course 1 — Foundations

::: {.card-grid}

::: {.card}
::: {.kicker}
WEEK 3 · SESSION 1
:::
### [CLT explorer](https://github.com/CTTIR/courses/tree/main/shiny/clt-explorer/)
Pick a parent distribution and a sample size; watch the sampling
distribution of the mean tighten and turn Gaussian as *n* grows.
:::

::: {.card}
::: {.kicker}
WEEK 3 · SESSION 2
:::
### [Bootstrap CI explorer](https://github.com/CTTIR/courses/tree/main/shiny/bootstrap-ci/)
Pick a statistic, a population, n, and B. The app draws one sample,
resamples it B times, and gives a percentile CI you can compare to the
true value.
:::

::: {.card}
::: {.kicker}
WEEK 2 · SESSION 3
:::
### [Diagnostic-test calculator](https://github.com/CTTIR/courses/tree/main/shiny/diagnostic-test/)
Sliders for sensitivity, specificity, and prevalence; outputs the
2×2 table, PPV/NPV, likelihood ratios, and the PPV-vs-prevalence curve.
:::

:::

::: {.card}

### [Linear-model diagnostics](https://github.com/CTTIR/courses/tree/main/shiny/lm-diagnostics/)
Generate data with chosen slope and noise (and optional
heteroscedasticity / outliers); inspect the four diagnostic plots
side-by-side.

::: {.card}

### [Logistic regression explorer](https://github.com/CTTIR/courses/tree/main/shiny/logistic-explorer/)
Pick intercept and slope; the app simulates, fits, and shows the
fitted curve, ROC, apparent calibration in probability intervals, and Brier score.
:::

::: {.card}
::: {.kicker}
WEEK 2 · SESSION 1
:::
### [One-way ANOVA + contrasts](https://github.com/CTTIR/courses/tree/main/shiny/anova-contrasts/)
Pick the number of groups and within-group noise; the app shows the
boxplot, ANOVA table, and Tukey HSD pairwise comparisons.

## Course 3 — Design & Causal

::: {.card-grid}

::: {.card}
::: {.kicker}
WEEK 3 · SESSION 3
:::
### [DAG explorer](https://github.com/CTTIR/courses/tree/main/shiny/dag-explorer/)
Pick a pre-built DAG (confounder, mediator, collider, M-bias) or paste
your own. The app computes minimal sufficient adjustment sets via
`dagitty`.
:::

::: {.card}
::: {.kicker}
WEEK 2 · SESSION 1
:::
### [Missing-data simulator](https://github.com/CTTIR/courses/tree/main/shiny/missing-data-sim/)
Compare the bias of complete-case analysis under MCAR, MAR, and
MNAR mechanisms over many replications.
:::

::: {.card}
::: {.kicker}
WEEK 4 · SESSION 4
:::
### [SIR / SEIR simulator](https://github.com/CTTIR/courses/tree/main/shiny/sir-simulator/)
Pick R0, infectious period, population size, and initial infected.
The app integrates the ODEs and reports peak prevalence and the removed fraction
at the end of the simulation.
:::

:::

Compare selection and evaluation on the same folds with inner/outer CV,

::: {.card}

## Deploying to your Shiny Server

The apps assume a stock self-hosted Shiny Server with each app folder
served at a route matching its name. To deploy them all:

```bash
rsync -avz --exclude README.md shiny/ user@your-host:/srv/shiny-server/
sudo systemctl restart shiny-server
```

Restore the versions recorded in `renv.lock` in the server environment and
configure the service to use that library. Verify each app, HTTPS, process
limits, logs, and the reverse proxy before exposing a server to users. The
static-site checks do not deploy or qualify a Shiny service.

Once a server is available, replace the source links with its actual app URLs.
An iframe can embed a verified app endpoint in a lesson, subject to the host's
frame policy. Test its sizing and keyboard access in both articles and slides.
